sa: अपि चात्र सनत्कुमारगीताः श्लोका भवन्ति-ब्रह्मा विश्वं सृजत् पूर्वं सर्वादिर्निरवस्कृतम्। ब्रह्मघोषैर्दिवं गच्छन्त्यमरा ब्रह्मयोनयः॥ ब्राह्मणानां मतिर्वाक्यं कर्म श्रद्धां तपांसि च। धारयन्ति महीं द्यां च शैक्यो वागमृतं तथा॥
en: Regarding it there is a Verse sung by Sanatkumara. Brahman, in creating the universe, first created the Brahmanas. The Brahmanas become immortal by studying the Vedas, and go to heaven by virtue of such study. The intelligence, speech, acts and observances, faith, and the penances of the Brahmanas keep up both the Earth and the heaven like slings of strings upholding bovine nectar.

sa: पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि अन्तरिक्षचराणि च। नद्यो ह्रदास्तडागाश्च सर्वप्रस्रवणानि च॥ उदपानानि वाप्यश्च तीर्थान्यायतनानि च। नि:संशयममावास्यां समेष्यन्ति नराधिप॥ मासि मासि नरव्याघ्र संनिहत्यां च संशयः। तीर्थसंनिहनादेव संनिहत्येति विश्रुता॥
en: Whatever Tirtha exists on earth or in the sky, all the rivers, lakes, ponds, springs, large and small tanks and all other Tirtha sacred to particular gods, O ruler of men, all come here without doubt on the day of new moon, And they certainly mix with Sannihati every month. It is therefore that this Tirtha is known by the name of Sannihati.

sa: शङ्कुभिर्दारिताः केचित् सम्भिन्नाश्च परश्वधैः॥ हस्तिभिर्मुदिताः केचित् क्षुण्णाश्चान्ये तुरंगमैः। रथनेमिनिकृत्ताश्च निकृत्ताश्च परश्वधैः॥ व्याक्रोशन्त नरा राजंस्तत्र तत्र स्म बान्धवान्। पुत्रानन्ये पितृनन्ये भ्रातृ॑श्च सह बन्धुभिः॥ मातुलान् भागिनेयांश्च परानपि च संयुगे।
en: Some pierced by javelins, some cut down by battle-axes, some crushed by elephants, some trodden down by horses, some cut by the car-wheels and some by axes, O king, loudly called for their kinsmen. Some called upon their sons, some upon their fathers, some upon their brothers some upon their relatives, some upon their maternal uncles, some upon their sister's sons, and some upon their friends and others.

sa: निरीक्ष्य स मुहूर्तं तु ददर्श भरतो गुरुम्। उटजे राममासीनं जटामण्डलधारिणम्॥ कृष्णाजिनधरं तं तु चीरवल्कलवाससम्। ददर्श राममासीनमभितः पावकोपमम्॥ सिंहस्कन्धं महाबाहुं पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम्। पृथिव्याः सागरान्ताया भर्तारं धर्मचारिणम्॥ उपविष्टं महाबाहुं ब्रह्माणमिव शाश्वतम्। स्थण्डिले दर्भसंस्तीर्णे सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च॥
en: And looking around, anon Bharata saw his superior Rāma seated in the cottage bearing a head of matted locks, clad in a black deer-skin, and having tattered cloth and bark for his garment. And he saw Råma seated like to a flame, with leonine shoulders, mighty arms, and eyes resembling lotuses, the righteous lord of this world bounded by the seas, saw the mightyarmed on like to the eternal Brahma, seated on a skin-seat on the ground along with Sītā and Lakş mana.

sa: ये चान्नमिच्छन्ति ददस्व तेभ्यः परिश्रिता ये परितो मनुष्याः। मधु चतुर्धा मम चात्मनश्च॥ अर्धं तु भीमाय च देहि भद्रे य एष नागर्षभतुल्यरूपः। गौरो युवा संहननोपपन्न एषो हि वीरो बहुभुक् सदैव॥
en: Feed (also) those that are hungry and give it to those that are our guests. Divide the rest into two portions. O amiable girl, give the half to Bhima, for this strong youth with fair complexion, a man like a king of elephants, this hero always eats much. Divide the other half into six equal parts, four for these youths (Yudhishthira, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva) one for myself and the other for you.

sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन् दशार्हाधितौ प्रयाते युधिष्ठिरो भीमसेनार्जुनौ च। यमौ च कृष्णा च पुरोहितश्च रथान् महार्हान् परमाश्वयुक्तान्॥ आस्थाय वीराः सहिता वनाय प्रतस्थिरे भूतपतिप्रकाशाः। हिरण्यनिष्कान् वसनानि गाश्च प्रदाय शिक्षाक्षरमन्त्रविद्यः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: When the chief of the Dasharhas had gone away, Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva), Krishna (Draupadi) and the priest (Dhaumya) ascending costly chariots yoked with excellent horses, departed for another forest. The heroes, each looking like the lord of spirits (Shiva,) distributed (at the time of their departure) Nishkas of gold, cloth and kine to the Brahmanas, learned in Sikha, Akshara and Mantras.

sa: भीष्म उवाच स मोक्षमनुचिन्त्यैव शुकः पितरमभ्यगात्। प्राहाभिवाद्य च गुरुं श्रेयोऽर्थी विनयान्वितः॥ मोक्षधर्मेषु कुशलो भगवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे। यथा मे मनसः शान्तिः परमा सम्भवेत् प्रभो॥
en: Bhishma said “Thinking of Liberation, Shuka approached his father, and possessed as he was of humility and desirous of acquiring his highest good, he saluted his great preceptor and said,-You are well-versed in the Religion of Liberation. Do you, O illustrious one, describe it to me, so that I may enjoy supreme tranquillity of mind, O powerful one.

sa: संस्मृत्य कालवाक्यानि ततो दुःखमुपागमत्। दुःखेन च सुसंतप्तः स्मृत्वा तद्धोरदर्शनम्॥ अवाङ्मुखो दीनमना व्याहतुं न शशाक ह। ततो बुद्ध्या विनिश्चित्य कालवाक्यानि राघवः। नैतदस्तीति निश्चित्य तूष्णीमासीन्ग्रहायशाः॥
en: There upon remembering the words of Kāla, Rāma was greatly sorry. And thinking of those dreadful words he was overwhelmed with grief. And with a poorly heart, and face downwards he remained silent for some time. There upon thinking of Kāla's words and determining that every calamity would befall him, that highly illustrious descendant, of Raghus, summoned patience.

sa: राजमार्गे ययौ रामो मध्येनागुरुधूपितम्। चन्दनानां च मुख्यानामगुरुणां च संचयैः॥ उत्तमानां च गन्धानां क्षौमकौशाम्बरस्य च। अविद्धाभिश्च मुक्ताभिरुत्तमैः स्फाटिकैरपि॥ शोभमानमसम्बाधं तं राजपथमुत्तमम्। संवृतं विविधैः पुष्पैर्भक्ष्यैरुच्चावचैरपि॥ ददर्श तं राजपथं दिवि देवपतिर्यथा। दध्यक्षतहविलाजैधूपैरगुरुचन्दनैः॥
en: It was a splendidly spacious road decorated with a coilection of sandal, Agaru and other fine scents, with silk and red cloth, with pearls holed and other valuable crystals and strewn with various flowers and filled with edibles multiform. Like to the lord of celestials in heaven he saw this high way and the court-yard covered with curd, clarified butter, fried paddy, Dhüpa, Agaru and sandal, and embellished with garlands and other scents.

sa: एते रथा नरव्याघ्राः सर्वशस्त्रसमन्विताः। धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राणां विमलाः काञ्चनध्वजाः॥ सस्वनानधिरोहध्वं नित्यसज्जानिमान् रथान्। इन्द्रसेनादिभिः सूतैः कृतशस्त्रैरधिष्ठितान्॥ एतानास्थाय वै यत्ता गन्धर्वान् यो माहवे। सुयोधनस्य मोक्षाय प्रयतध्वमतन्द्रिताः॥ य एव कश्चिद् राजन्यः शरणार्थमिहागतम्। परं शक्त्याभिरक्षेत किं पुनस्त्वं वृकोदर॥
en: These blazing cars with golden flag-staffs belonging to the son of Dhritarashtra are now all ready (before you). With Indrasena and other charioteers who are all skilled in arms, ride all of you these ever furnished cars with deep rattling noise. Ride on them and fight to your utmost power with the Gandharvas to rescue Duryodhana. Even an ordinary Kshatriya would try his best to protect one who has come to him for protection. What then, O Vrikodara, shall I speak to you?

sa: व्यास उवाच वेत्थ धर्मं सत्यवति परं चापरमेव च॥ तथा तव महाप्राज्ञे धर्मे प्रणिहिता मतिः। तस्मादहं त्वन्नियोगाद् धर्ममुद्दिश्य कारणम्॥ ईप्सितं ते करिष्यामि दृष्टं ह्येतत् सनातनम्। भ्रातुः पुत्रान् प्रदास्यामि मित्रावरुणयोः समान्॥
en: Vyasa said: O (mother) Satyavati, you know what is virtue, both as regards this world and the next. O lady of great wisdom, your mind is also fixed on virtue. Therefore, making virtue my motive, I shall, at your command, do what you desire, knowing (as I do) that this practice is conformable to the true and eternal religion. I shall produce for my brother sons that will be like Yama and Varuna.

sa: जनमेजय उवाच धर्मात्मनि महावीर्ये सत्यसंधे जितात्मनि। देवव्रते महाभागे शरतल्पगतेऽच्युते॥ शयाने वीरशयने भीष्मे शान्तनुनन्दने। गाङ्गेये पुरुषव्याघ्र पाण्डवैः पर्युपासिते॥ काः कथाः समवर्तन्त तस्मिन् वीरसमागमे। हतेषु सर्वसैन्येषु तन्मे शंस महामुने॥
en: Janamejaya said When that foremost men, of righteous soul and great energy, strictly devoted to truth and with passions restrained, viz., the son of Shantanu and Ganga, named Devavrata or Bhishma of undecaying glory, lay on a hero's bed with the sons of Pandu sitting around him, tell me, O great sage, what conversation took place in that meeting of heroes after the destruction of all the soldiers.

sa: विद्यां श्रुत्वा ये गुरुं नाद्रियन्ते प्रत्यासन्ना मनसा कर्मणा वा। तेषां पापं भ्रूणहत्याविशिष्टं नान्यस्तेभ्यः पापकृदस्ति लोके। यथैव ते गुरुभिर्भावनीर्या स्तथा तेषां गुरवोऽभ्यर्चनीयाः॥
en: They, who do not honour their preceptors after receiving instruction from them by obeying them dutifully in thought and deed commit the sin of killing a foetus. There is no greater sinner in this world than this. Preceptors always treat their disciples with great affection. The latter should, therefore, reverse their preceptors duly.

sa: तं विदित्वा गतक्रोधं भीमसेनवधार्दितम्। वासुदेवो वरः पुंसामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ मा शुचो धृतराष्ट्रं त्वं नैष भीमस्त्वया हतः। आयसी प्रतिमा ह्येषा त्वया निष्पातिता विभो॥
en: Knowing that he was no longer under the influence of anger, and that he was truly sorry for having (as he believed) slain Bhima, Vasudeva, that foremost of men, said,-'Do not grieve, O Dhritarashtra, for you have not killed Bhimasena. That is an iron statue, O king, whica has been broken by you.

sa: प्रत्ययार्थं ततः सीता विवेश ज्वलनं तदा। प्रत्यक्षं तव सौमित्रे देवानां हव्यवाहनः॥ अपापां मैथिलीमाह वायुश्चाकाशगोचरः। चन्द्रादित्यौ च शंसेते सुराणां संनिधौ पुरा ॥
en: To secure my confidence, Sītā, in your very presence, entered fire. At that time, O Saumitri, fire, carrying sacrificial oblations and the wind of the sky declared Sītā's innocence before the celestials. in the presence of all the Rşis and gods, the Sun and Moon announced the innocence of the daughter of Janaka.

sa: द्रोण उवाच प्रार्थयामि त्वया सख्यं पुनरेव नराधिप। अराजा किल नो राज्ञः सखा भवितुमर्हति॥ अतः प्रयतितं राज्ये यज्ञसेन त्वया सह। राजासि दक्षिणे कूले भागीरथ्याहमुत्तरे॥
en: Drona said: O king, I again solicit your friendship. He who is not a king should not be a friend of a king. Therefore, O Yajnasena, I shall divide this kingdom amongst ourselves. You will be the king of the country lying on the south banks of the Bhagirathi and I shall be that on the north banks.

sa: देवा ऊचुः ऋणिनो मानवा ब्रह्मन् जायन्ते तेन तच्छृणु। क्रियाभिर्ब्रह्मचर्येण प्रजया च न संशयः॥ तदपाक्रियते सर्वं यज्ञेन तपसा श्रुतैः। तपस्वी यज्ञकृच्चासि न च ते विद्यते प्रजा॥
en: The Celestial said: O Brahmana, hear of those acts and things for which men are bom debtors. There is no doubt that men are born debtors for Kriya, religious rites, for Brahmacharya, study according to the ordinance and for progeny. These debts are discharged by scarifies, asceticism and offspring. You are an ascetic, you have also performed scarifies, but you have no offspring.

sa: मन्त्रिणो भ्रातरश्चान्ये तद्वचः प्रत्यपूजयन्। स तु राजा महाप्राज्ञः पुनरेवात्मनाऽऽत्मवान्॥ ते तेन राज्ञा भूयो विममृशे पार्थो लोकानां हितकाम्यया। सामर्थ्ययोगं सम्प्रेक्ष्य देशकालौ व्ययागमौ॥
en: His ministers and his brothers highly approved of his words. The greatly wise and self-controlled son of Pritha (Yudhishthira), ever desirous to do good to the world, again thought over the matter in his mind, taking into his consideration his won strength and means, the time and the place, his income and expenditure.

sa: स्वागतं ते द्विजश्रेष्ठ यदिच्छसि वदस्व मे। एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण भारद्वाजोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥ रामं प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठं दित्सन्तं विविधं वसु। अहं धनमनन्तं हि प्रार्थये विपुलव्रत॥
en: "O best of the twice born, you are welcome. Tell me what you desire.” Having been thus addressed by (Parashu) Rama, the son of Bharadvaja (Drona) said to that foremost of all smiters, Rama, who was desirous of giving away all his wealth, “O (Rishi) of multifarious vows, I ask your eternal। wealth."

sa: बलं च सुभृतं वीर हृष्टतुष्टमनुद्धतम्। संभाषासंप्रदानेन रञ्जयस्व नरोत्तम॥ न ह्यास्तत्र तिष्ठन्ति न दारा न च बान्धवाः। सुप्रीतो भृत्यवर्गस्तु यत्र तिष्ठति राघव॥
en: Do you so act, O hero, that soldiers might be well-fed and delighted and be not annoyed with you. Do you please them with sweet words, for the servants, when they face enemies, have not with them friends or wives—and so they are pleased, O Rāghava when they receive sufficient food and presents.

sa: अवसं वै ब्राह्मणच्छद्मनाहं रामे पुरा दिव्यमस्त्रं चिकीर्षुः। तत्रापि मे देवराजेन विघ्नो हितार्थिना फाल्गुनस्यैव शल्य॥ कृतो विभेदेन ममोरुमेत्य प्रविश्य कीटस्य तनुं विरूपाम्। ममोरुमेत्य प्रबिभेद कीट: सुप्ते गुरौ तत्र शिरो निधाय॥
en: I lived formerly with Rama in the disguise of a Brahmana with a view to obtain the celestial weapons from him. At that time, O Shalya, the king of gods, wishing to do a good office by Phalguna, put in an impediment by approaching my thigh and piercing it in the form of a dreadful worm. When my preceptor slept placing his head on my thigh that worm began to bore it through.

sa: व्यस्मयन्त रणे योधा देवताश्च समागताः। ततः शरसहस्रेण शतचन्द्रमपातयत्॥ चर्म खङ्गं च सम्बाधे धृष्टद्युम्नस्य स द्विजः। ये तु वैतस्तिका नाम शरा आसन्नयोधिनः॥
en: All the warriors present as also the celestials, were filled with amazement. The twice-born Drona then discharging a thousand arrows in the press of the battle, cut-off Dhristadyumna's sword and shield covered with hundred moons. The arrows that Drona shot in that fight in close quarters were of the length of a span.

sa: तत्र भोगवती नाम सर्पाणामालयः पुरी॥ विशालरथ्य दुर्धर्षा सर्वतः परिरक्षिता। रक्षिता पन्नगै।रैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्महाविषैः॥ सर्पराजो महाघोरो यस्यां वसति वासुकिः। निर्याय मार्गितव्या च सा च भोगवती पुरी॥
en: In it also there is that palace, which is the abode of snakes; having spacious ways, i incapable of being captured, guarded around, and protected by dreadful snakes and sharptoothed serpents of virulent poison; where dwelleth Vāsuki, the exceedingly terrible king of snakes. Proceeding heedfully, you must explore that Bhogavatī palace; also whatever concealed place may lie there.

sa: तुष्टेन तेन दत्तौ ते द्वौ वरौ शुभदर्शने। स त्वयोक्तः पतिर्देवि यदिच्छेयं तदा वरम्॥ गृह्णीयां तु तदा भर्तस्तथेत्युक्तं महात्मना । अनभिज्ञा ह्यहं देवि त्वयैव कथितं पुरा॥ कथैषा तव तु स्नेहान्मनसा धार्यते मया। रामाभिषेकसम्भारान्निगृह्य विनिवर्तय॥
en: Thereupon gratified, he, O, you of gracious presence, granted you two boons. Whereupon you did say, 'I shall receive from my lord the boon whenever I shall wish. Thereupon that high-souled one said., 'So be it? I did not know anything about this, O respected one; and it was you who did formerly communicate this (to me.) And it is because I bear affection to you that I have not forgotten it. Now do you forcibly make the monarch desist from installing Rāma.

sa: पुण्यश्च रमणीयश्च बहुमूलफलायुतः। तत्र कुञ्जरयूथानि मृगयूथानि चैव हि ॥ विचरन्ति वनान्तेषु तानि द्रक्ष्यसि राघव। सरित्प्रस्रवणप्रस्थान् दरीकन्दरनिर्झरान्। चरतः सीतया सार्धं नन्दिष्यति मनस्तव।॥
en: Do you repair to the famed Citrakuţa, holy, fair to the view, and abounding in countless fruits and roots. And in those forests range herds of elephants and deer; and these, O Rāghava, you will behold. And ranging with Sītā rivers and rills and plateau's, caverns and fountains, your mind will experience delight.

sa: नरैरिवोल्काभिरपोह्यमानो महागजो ध्वान्तमभिप्रविष्टः। भूयः प्रजज्वाल विलापमेवं निशम्य रामः करुणं जनन्याः॥ मार्तं च सौमित्रिमभिप्रतप्तम्। धर्मे स्थितो धर्म्यमुवाच वाक्यं यथा स एवार्हति तत्र वक्तुम् ॥
en: Hearing these sorrowful words of his mother, Rāma was again inflamed with ire, like to an clephant goaded with a fire-brand, when entering into darkness. He, abiding in righteousness spoke such pious words to his mother, almost insensible, and to the son of Sumitrā, bewailing and racked with sorrow, as he was justified to utter on that occasion.

sa: अस्याश्च नद्याः कल्याणि वद सत्यमनिन्दिते। साव्रवीत् तानृपीन् नाहमरण्यस्यास्य देवता॥ न चाप्यस्य गिरेविप्रा नैव नद्याश्च देवता। मानुषीं मां विजानीत यूयं सर्वे तपोधनाः॥
en: She said unto the sages, “O twice-born ones! neither am I the deity of this forest, nor the goddess of this mountain, nor of this river. Know me for a daughter of human beings, O you sages of ascetic wealth! I am relating my history in detail, do you listen attentively to me.

sa: तीर्थे चात्र सरः पुण्यं वसूनां भरतर्षभ। तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च वसूनां सम्मतो भवेत्॥ सिन्धूत्तममिति ख्यातं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्। तत्र स्नात्वा नरश्रेष्ठ लभेद् बहु सुवर्णकम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, in that Tirtha there is a lake of the Vasus. Bathing in it and drinking its water, one becomes respected of the Vasus. O foremost of men, it is known by the name of Sindhuttama and it destroys all sins. Bathing in it one obtains (the fruits of giving away) much gold.

sa: रथघोषं तु तं श्रुत्वा हयसंग्रहणं च तत्। वार्ष्णेयश्चिन्तयामास बाहुकस्य हयज्ञताम्॥ किं नु स्यान्मातलिरयं देवराजस्य सारथिः। तथा तल्लक्षणं वीरे बाहुके दृश्यते महत्॥
en: Varshneya, hearing the sound of the car (of its wheels) and witnessing the management of the horses, was set to thinking on the knowledge of Bahuka in the science of steeds. He said, “Was he not Matali, the charioteer of the king of the gods? That auspicious mark is seen in heroic Bahuka.

sa: कन्योवाच देवदानवयक्षाणां किन्नरोरगरक्षसाम्। जेता यो दुष्टदैत्यानां महावीर्यो महाबलः॥ यस्तु सर्वाणि भूतानि त्वया सह विजेष्यति। स हि मे भविता भर्ता ब्रह्मण्यः कीर्तिवर्धनः॥
en: Devasena said : That mighty, celebrated and powerful being who will be ever devoted to Brahma, who will be able to conquer the Devas, the Danavas, the Yakshas, the Kinnaras, the Nagas, the Rakshashas and the evil minded Daityas and who will be able to subjugate all the worlds, should be my husband.

sa: सोऽपश्यदासीनमुपेत्य पुत्रं ध्यायन्तमेकं विपरीतचित्तम्। विनिःश्वसन्तं मुहुरूर्ध्वदृष्टिं विभाण्डकः पुत्रमुवाच दीनम्॥ न कल्प्यन्ते समिधः किं नु तात कच्चिद्भुतं चाग्निहोत्रं त्वयाद्य। सुनिर्णिक्तं झुक्नुवं होमधेनुः कच्चित् सवत्साद्य कृता त्वया च॥ न वै यथापूर्वमिवासि पुत्र चिन्तापरश्चासि विचेतनश्च। दीनोऽतिमात्रं त्वमिहाद्य किं नु पृच्छामि त्वां क इहाद्यागतोऽभूत्॥
en: He came up and saw his son seated alone, pensive and sad and dejected. He was sighing again and again with upturned eyes. Vibhandaka thus spoke to his distressed son, "O child, why do you not hew logs for the sacrificial fire? I hope you have performed today the Agnihotra (fire sacrifice). I hope you have polished the sacrificial ladles and spoons and brought out the sacrificial cow with her calf, O son, you are not in your wonted state today. You are pensive and absent minded. Why are you so much distressed today? I ask you, who came here today?

sa: तदेतत् कारणं राजन् यदहं नागसाह्वयम्। नागमं परवीरन न हि जीवेत् सुयोधनः॥ मय्यागतेऽथवा वीर द्यूतं न भविता तथा। अद्याहं किं करिष्यामि भिन्नसेतुरिवोदकम्॥
en: O king, O slayer of hostile heroes, this is the reason why I could not come to Hastinapur. If I had come Duryodhana would not have been alive and the gambling match would not have taken place. What can I do today? It is difficult stop the water when the dam is broken."

sa: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र भीमायाः स्थानमुत्तमम्। तत्र सषत्वा तु योन्यां वै नरो भरतसत्तम॥ देव्याः पुत्रो भवेद् राजंस्तप्तकुण्डलविग्रहः। गवां शतसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः॥
en: O king of kings, one should then go to the excellent region of Bhima. O best of the Bharata race, bathing there in Yoni (Tirtha) a man. Becomes, O king, a son of a goddess, adorned with earring set with pearls. That man also obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine.

sa: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा दीनो दुःशासनोऽब्रवीत्। अश्रुकण्ठः सुदुःखार्तः प्राञ्जलिः प्रणिपत्य च॥ सगद्गदमिदं वाक्यं भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठमात्मनः। प्रसीदेत्यपतद् भूमौ दूयमानेन चेतसा॥ दुःखितः पादयोस्तस्य नेत्रजं जलमुत्सृजन्। उक्तवांश्च नरव्याघ्रो नैतदेवं भविष्यति॥
en: Having heard his words, Dushasana in great misery and grief said to his eldest brother with joined hands, with bent down head and with voice choked in tears, “Relent.” Saying this, he fell down on the earth in the greatest possible misery. In sorrow and grief that foremost of men shed tears on the feet of his brother and thus spoke to him, “This can never be done.

sa: तत उत्थाय कैकेयी सर्वास्ताः प्रत्यभाषत। प्रेष्याः समुत्थिताश्चापि कैकेयीं ताः स्त्रियोऽब्रुवन्॥ प्रेक्ष्य मामनवद्यागी कश्मलोपहतामिव। स्नेहात् संवासजाद् धर्मात् सूदमेषा शुचिस्मिता॥ योद्ध्यमानं महावीर्यमियं समनुशोचति। कल्याणरूपा सैरन्ध्री बल्लवश्चापि सुन्दरः॥ स्त्रीणां चित्तं च दुर्जेयं युक्तरूपौ च मे मतौ। सैरन्ध्री प्रियसंवासान्नित्यं करुणवादिनी॥ अस्मिन् राजकुले चेमौ तुल्यकालनिवासिनौ। इति ब्रुवाणा वाक्यानि सा मां नित्यमतर्जयत्॥
en: Then rising from her seat along with her maids who also rose up with her, Kaikayi beholding me with limbs uninjured and only overtaken by swoon, addressed them saying "surely it is from the affection originated by living together that this lady of beautiful smile grieves for the cook, seeing him fighting with beasts of exceeding strength. Sairandhri is one of exceeding beauty and Ballava is handsome too, the heart of woman is so hard to know; and me-thinks they both are deserving of each other. Sairandhri is seen constantly lamenting for the connection with her lover and they both have entered this royal family at the same time.” Speaking such words she always scolds me.

sa: तस्मादर्थागमाः सर्वे मनोमोहविवर्धनाः। कार्पण्यं दर्पमानौ च भयमुद्वेग एव च॥ अर्थजानि विदुः प्राज्ञा दुःखान्येतानि देहिनाम्। अर्थस्योत्पादने चैव पालने च तथा क्षये।॥ सहन्ति च महद् दुःखं प्रन्ति चैवार्थकारणात्। अर्था दुःखं परित्यक्तुं पालिताश्चैव शत्रवः॥
en: Therefore, the accession of wealth is what increases covetousness and folly. It is the root of niggardliness, boastfulness, pride, fear and anxiety. These are the miseries that wise men see in wealth. Men have to suffer infinite miseries in the acquisition and retention of wealth. Its expenditure also is painful. Sometimes men are even killed for the sake of wealth. To abandon wealth is painful; even those men who are cherished become enemies for the sake of wealth.

sa: वासुदेव उवाच रोदिष्यन्ति स्त्रियो ह्येव येषां क्रुद्धासि भाविनि। बीभत्सुशरसंच्छन्नाञ्छोणितौघपरिप्लुतान्॥ निहतान् वल्लभान् वीक्ष्य शयानान् वसुधातले। यत् समर्थं पाण्डवानां तत् करिष्यामि मा शुचः।।
en: Krishna said: O fair lady, the wives of those with whom you are angry will weep like you on seeing their husbands lying dead on the ground, their bodies covered with the arrows of Vivatsu and weltering in blood. Do not grieve; I shall do for the Pandavas whatever lies in my power.

sa: कालरात्रिनिभा ह्यासीद् घोररूपा भयानका। शिखण्डी तु महाराज गौतमस्य महद् धनुः॥ अर्धचन्द्रेण चिच्छेद सज्यं सविशिखं तदा। तस्य क्रुद्धः कृपो राजशक्तिं चिक्षेप दारुणाम्॥
en: That awfully-dreadful night striking terror (into very heart) seemed to be the death-night (of all the combatants). Then, O great monarch, Shikandi cut-off the great bow of the son of Goutama with a crescent-shaped (dart) and poured down sharpened arrows (at him). Kripa, then, O monarch, excited with rage, hurled a formidable dart.

sa: ततः स लब्ध्वा तां भार्यां वरुणं प्राह धर्मवित्। उतथ्यः सुमहातेजा यत् तच्छृणु नराधिप॥ मयैषा तपसा प्राप्ता क्रोशतस्ते जलाधिप। इत्युक्त्वा तामुपादाय स्वमेव भवनं ययौ॥
en: Knowing every duty, the highly energetic Rishi Utathya, after getting back his wife, O king, said to Varuna, I have recovered my wife, O lord of waters, with the help of my penances and after inflicting such distress on you as made you cry aloud in pain. Having said this, he went home, with that wife of his.

sa: शिष्याणां वचनं श्रुत्वा पराशरसुतः प्रभुः। प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्॥ क्षितिं वा देवलोकं वा गम्यतां यदि रोचते। अप्रमादश्च वः कार्यो ब्रह्म हि प्रचुरच्छलम्॥
en: Hearing these words of his disciples, the powerful son of Parashara, replied them in these wholesome words which were fraught, besides, with virtue and profit.-You may go to the Earth or to the regions of the gods as ye like. You should always be careful, for the Vedas are such that they are always liable to be misunderstood.

sa: संजय उवाच ततो व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु तावकेषु परेषु च। धनंजयो स्थानीकमवधीत् तव भारत॥ शरैरतिरथो युद्धे दारयन् रथयूथपान्। ते वध्यमानाः पार्थेन कालेनेव युगक्षय॥ धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे यत्नात् पाण्डवान् प्रत्ययोधयन्। प्रार्थयाना यशो दीप्तं मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्॥ एकाग्रमनसो भूत्वा पाण्डवानां वरूथिनीम्। बभञ्जुर्बहुशो राजंस्ते चासज्जन्त संयुगे॥
en: Sanjaya said When your troops and those of the Pandavas were placed in battle array, that great car-warrior Dhananjaya made a great slaughter by cutting down with his arrows many leaders of car-warriors; your troops though thus slaughtered in the battle by the son of Pritha who resembled the destroyer himself at the end of a Yuga, yet fought with the Pandavas with perseverance. Desiring to win blazing glory and making death their final goal with minds undirected to anything else, they broke the Pandava ranks in many places, but their ranks also were in many places broken.

sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा तत्र त्वरितं गत्वा घूर्णिकासुरमन्दिरम्॥ दृष्ट्वा काव्यमुवाचेदं सम्भ्रमाविष्टचेतना। आचचक्षे महाप्राज्ञं देवयानी वने हताम्॥ शर्मिष्ठया महाभाग दुहित्रा वृषपर्वणः। श्रुत्वा दुहितरं काव्यस्तत्र शर्मिष्ठया हताम्॥ त्वरया निर्ययौ दुःखान्मार्गमाणः सुतां वने। दृष्ट्वा दुहितरं काव्यो देवयानीं ततो वने॥ बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। आत्मदोषैर्नियच्छन्ति सर्वे दुःखसुखे जनाः॥ मन्ये दुश्चरितं तेऽस्ति यस्येयं निष्कृतिः कृता।
en: Vaishampayana said: Ghurnika speedily went to the palace of the Asura (chief). Finding the son of Kavi (Shukra), she spoke to his thus, her perception having been dimmed by anger. “O great Brahmana, O illustrious man, I tell you, Devayani had been ill-used by Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparva. Having heard that his daughter had been ill-used by Sharmishtha, he soon went to search for her with a heavy heart. And when he found her in the forest, the son of Kavi embraced her with affection and spoke to her with his voice choked with grief. “The weal and woe that befall on people is always due to their own faults. You had some fault, I am sure, which has been thus expiated."

sa: अथ प्रस्थाप्य स हरीन् सुग्रीवो दक्षिणां दिशम्। अब्रवीन्मेघसंकाशं सुषेणं नाम वानरम्॥ तारायाः पितरं राजा श्वशुरं भीमविक्रमम्। अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिवाक्यमभिगम्य प्रणम्य च॥ महर्षिपुत्रं मारीचमर्चिष्मन्तं महाकपिम्। वृतं कपिवरैः शूरैर्महेन्द्रसदृशद्युतिम्॥ बुद्धिविक्रमसम्पन्नं वैनतेयसमद्युतिम्। मरीचिपुत्रान् मारीचानचिर्माल्यान् महाबलान्॥ ऋषिपुत्रांश्च तान् सर्वान्प्रतीचीमादिशद् दिशम्। द्वाभ्यां शतसहस्राभ्यां कपीनां कपिसत्तमाः॥ सुषेणप्रमुखा यूयं वैदेही परिमार्गथ।
en: Having despatched those monkeys in a southern direction, Sugrīva spoke to the monkey named Susena, resembling a mass of clouds. Approaching his father-in-law, Tara's father, possessed of dreadful prowess, the king, bowing and with joined hands, spoke to him. And Sugriva commanded the Maharsi's son, Marica, and the mighty ape Archishmat, surrounded by the heroic foremost of monkeys,-possessing the splendour of Mahendra, gifted with sense and vigour; and resembling the offspring himself of Vinată in brightness; and Mārīci's son,-the Mārīcas—the mighty Archirmālyas,-all these sons of the saint*. (to march) towards the West, saying,-You monkey-chiefs, let twice hundred thousand monkeys led by Sușeņa (set out) to search Vaidehi. Märīci.

sa: साध्याश्च विश्वे मरुतो वाद्यानि सुमहान्ति च। नद्यः शैला: समुद्राश्च तीर्थानि विविधानि च।॥ तपांसि संयोगविधिर्वेदाः स्तोभाः सरस्वती। नारदः पर्वतश्चैव विश्वावसुर्हहाहुहूः॥ गन्धर्वश्चित्रसेनश्च परिवारगणैर्युतः। नागाः सिद्धाश्च मुनयो देवदेवः प्रजापतिः॥ विष्णुः सहस्रशीर्षश्च देवोऽचिन्त्यः समागमत्। अवाद्यन्तान्तरिक्षे च भेर्यस्तूर्याणि वा विभो॥
en: The Sadhyas, the Vishvas, the Mantras, various sorts of loud and sweet music, the Rivers, the Mountains, the Seas, the Sacred Waters, the Penances, the Ordinances about Yoga, the Vedas, the Sounds accompanying the singing of the Samans, Sarasvati, Narada, Parvata, Vishvavasu, the Hahas, the Huhus, the are Gandharva Chitrasena with all the members of his family, the Nagas, the Siddhas, the Munis, the god of gods, viz., Prajapati, and the inconceivable and thousand-headed Vishnu himself, came there. Drums and trumpets were beat and blown in the sky.

sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रविशन्नर्जुनो राजन्नाश्रमं सत्यवादिनः। ददर्शासीनमेकान्ते मुनि सत्यवतीसुतम्॥
en: As Arjuna entered the hermitage of the truthful Rishi, he saw the son of Satyavati seated in a solitary spot.

sa: ततो युधिष्ठिरस्तेषां श्रृण्वतां मधुसूदनम्। अब्रवीत् पुण्डरीकाक्षमाभाष्य मधुरं वचः॥
en: Thereafter king Yudhishthira, at the hearing of those assembled Kshatriyas, said these sweet words addressing that slayer of Madhu, who

sa: भयेन महताऽऽविष्टो हृदि शोकेन चाहतः। पाञ्चालराजो दयितां मातरं वै शिखण्डिनः॥
en: Being filled, as the Panchala king was, with great fear and struck with grief at his heart, he said to the beloved mother of Shikhandin.

sa: स तु तेन प्रहारेण पीडितः प्रमुमोह वै। स्त्रस्तगात्रो महाबाहुर्धनरुत्सृज्य स्यन्दने॥
en: Greatly assailed by the violence of that spike the powerful Karna, with weaked limbs, swooned away on his car his bow dropping from his hand.

sa: मनसो दुःखमूलं तु स्नेह इत्युपलभ्यते। स्नेहात् तु सज्जते जन्तुर्दुःखयोगमुपैति च॥
en: It appears attachment is the root of all mental agonies; it is attachment that makes every creature miserable and brings on every kind of woe.

sa: ततः कृतस्वस्त्ययना राज्यलम्भाय पार्थिवाः। कृत्वा सर्वाणि कार्याणि प्रययुर्वारणावतम्॥
en: Having performed propitiatory rites for obtaining the kingdom and making all other preparations, the princes (the Pandavas) started for Varanavata.

sa: बभूग्रसेनयो राज्यं नाप्तुं शक्यं कथंचन। ज्ञातिभेदभयात् कृष्ण त्वया चापि विशेषतः॥
en: The kingdom cannot be taken back from Babhru and Ugrasena. You, O Krishna, cannot, in particular, take it back from fear of creating intestine feuds.

sa: प्रजाः सृजेति चादिष्टः पूर्वं दक्षः स्वयम्भुवा। असृजद् वृत्तिमेवाग्रे प्रजानां हितकाम्यया॥
en: Formerly the Selfcreate Brahman commanded the Rishi Daksha, saying, Do you create living creatures, For doing good to creatures, Daksha, first of all created food.

sa: ततः सागरपर्यन्तां भोक्ष्यसे मेदिनीमिमाम्। भ्रातृभिः सहितो वीर द्रौपद्या च सहानया॥
en: Then will you come into the possess of this world ending with the ocean, in company with your brothers, O hero and this lady Draupadi.

sa: यज्ञैरवाप्यते सोमः स च गोषु प्रतिष्ठितः। ततो देवाः प्रमोदन्ते पूर्वं वृत्तिस्ततः प्रजाः॥
en: It is by sacrifice that Soma is got. Sacrifice has been fixed upon kine. The gods become pleased through sacrifices. The means of livelihood were created first, creatures came next.

sa: ततः प्रत्यवहारोऽभूत् पाण्डवानां विशाम्पते। कौरवाणां च दीनानां द्रोणे युधि निपातिते॥
en: Thereupon, O ruler of men, the Pandava and the Kaurava troops were both withdrawn, the latter highly defeated in consequence of the overthrow of Drona.

sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच अभून्मुहूर्ते स्तिमितं सर्वं तद्राजमण्डलम्। तूष्णीभूते ततस्तस्मिन् पटे चित्रमिवार्पितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said When Bhishma became silent, the entire body of kings became perfectly silent. Indeed, they all sat motionless there, like figures painted on canvas.

sa: को हि तेषां समक्षं तान् हन्यादपि मरुत्पतिः॥ एतदीदृशकं वृत्तं राजन् सुप्तजने विभो।
en: Who is there, not even excluding the lord Indra, that can kill them before these heroes? Besides, O king Ashvatthaman could achieve this only because the men were all asleep.

sa: प्रविष्टः स महात्मानं भ्राता ते बुद्धिसत्तमः। दृष्ट्वा महात्मा कौन्तेयं महायोगबलान्वितः॥
en: Gifted with great Yoga-Power, your highsouled brother, that foremost of intelligent men, seeing the high-souled Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti has entered into his body.

sa: स रथो भ्राजतेऽत्यर्थमुह्यमानो रणे तदा। उह्यमानमिवाकाशे विमानं पाण्डुरैर्हयैः॥
en: That chariot, borne in that battle by white steeds, appeared excessively effulgent, like a celestial car borne through the firmament.

sa: न त्वेतदनुरूपं ते यशसो वा कुलस्य च। समृद्धार्थोऽसमृद्धार्थं यन्मां कस्थितुमिच्छसि॥
en: This conduct of yours, however, does not become your fame or birth. Yourself enjoying prosperity, you wish to mock me that am sunk in adversity.

sa: जयेत् कदर्यं दानेन सत्येनानृतवादिनम्। क्षमया क्रूरकर्माण-मसाधु साधुना जयेत्॥
en: One should conquer the mean by charity, the untruthful by truth, the wicked by forgiveness and the dishonest by honesty.

sa: गुह्यं चैतत् त्वया कार्यं नाख्यातव्यं शुभे क्वचित्। गत्वा नहुषमेकान्ते ब्रवीहि च सुमध्यमे॥
en: It should be done by you with secrecy and on no account should you give it out. O you of slender waist, go to Nahusha and speak thus to him.

sa: योऽसौ सर्वत्रगः श्रीमानक्षरात्मा व्यवस्थितः। तस्य प्रभावात् संक्षोभस्त्रिदिवस्य प्रकाशते॥
en: This heaven has been agitated from the prowess of the illustrious being, who is omnipresent, eternal and the never-perishing soul.

sa: ततः समभवद् युद्धं मम तस्य च भारत। तुमुलं सर्वभूतानां लोमहर्षणमद्भुतम्॥
en: Then begin that mighty battle between him and me, O Bharata, which was wonderful and which made the hairs of all creatures stand on end.

sa: यद् युगान्ते पशुपतिः सर्वभूतानि संहरन्। प्रयुङ्क्ते पुरुषव्याघ्र तदिदं मयि वर्तते॥
en: That (weapon) which the lord of all gods uses when he annihilates all forms of existence, even that O best among men, is with me.

sa: पर्वतः॥ ततो भरतशार्दूल घिष्ण्यमाकाशगं यथा। स मामभ्यवधीत् तूर्णं जत्रुदेशे कुरूद्वह॥
en: Then, O best among Kurus, it struck me on my shoulder, even then, O perpetuator of Kuru's race, like a lightning ranging in the sky.

sa: मातुश्च यौतकं यत् स्यात् कुमारीभाग एव सः। दौहित्र एव तद् रिक्थमपुत्रस्य पितुर्हरेत्॥
en: Whatever is the own property of the mother, is due to the maiden daughter. If the maternal grandfather happens to die without leaving sons, the daughter's son should inherit it.

sa: एष लोकान् ससर्जादौ देवांश्च ऋषिभिः सह। निधनं चैव मृत्युं च प्राजानां प्रभवाप्ययौ॥
en: At first, He created these worlds as also the celestials along with all the sages, He also created decrepitude and death of all creatures and also their growth and birth.

sa: सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम्। सुखदुःखे मनुष्याणां चक्रवत् परिवर्ततः॥
en: Sorrow comes after joy, and joy after sorrow. The joys and sorrows of human beings are revolving on a wheel.

sa: य एवं वर्तते नित्यं ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिमण्डले। मित्रेष्वमित्रे मध्यस्थे चिरं यशसि तिष्ठति॥
en: One who always conducts himself in this way with his kinsmen and relatives and treats thus his friends and enemies, succeeds in acquiring everlasting fame.'

sa: उत्सहन्तेऽन्यथा कर्तुमेतदस्रं मयेरितम्। तदिदं केवलं हत्वा शान्तमक्षौहिणी ज्वलत्॥
en: Dare baffle this weapon invoked by me. This weapon however has become pacified having slain only one Akshauhini of troops.

sa: न्यषीदत रथोपस्थे शिखण्डी रथिनां वरः। सीदन्तं चैनमालोक्य कृपः शारद्वतो युधि॥
en: Shikhandin, the foremost of car-warriors, sank down exhausted on the terrace of his car. Kripa, the son of Saradvata, seeing himself exhausted in that engagement.

sa: भीष्मोऽहमस्मि भद्रं ते दासोऽस्मि तव सुव्रत। तव संदर्शनादेव मुक्तोऽहं सर्वकिल्बिषैः॥
en: "O Rishi of excellent vows, be blessed; I am Bhishma, your servant. At the very sight of yours I am cleansed of all my sins."

sa: ईप्सितं ते करिष्यामि गच्छ पार्थाविचारयन्। नाहत्वा समरे द्रोणो धृष्टद्युम्नं कथञ्चन॥
en: “I will do, O Pritha's son, what you desire me to do. Go you with your heart at rest. Without slaying Dhrishtadyumna in battle, Drona.

sa: आकाशात् तु विकुर्वाणात् सर्वगन्धवहः शुचिः। बलवाञ्जायते वायुस्तस्य स्पर्शो गुणो मतः॥
en: From Ether, by modification, originates the bearer of all scents, viz., the pure, and powerful Wind. It is said to possess the property of Touch.

sa: तवार्जुनो नानुमते ब्रह्मबन्धो रणाजिरम्। प्रविष्टः स हि दुर्धर्षः शक्रस्यापि विशेद् बलम्॥ तेन वै परमां पूजां कुर्वता मानितो ह्यसि। नार्जुनोऽहं घृणी द्रोण भीमसेनोऽस्मि॥
en: And waxing worth, quickly replied to Drona with his eyes looking like burnished copper-"O vilest of Brahmanas, it cannot be that Arjuna has entered this array with your permission. He is invincible and is competent even to penetrate through the army of Shakra himself. It was only for honoring you that he offered you worship.

sa: अस्यां राजर्षिभिः पुत्रा जाता वै धार्मिकास्त्रयः। चतुर्थं जनयत्वेकं भवानपि नरोत्तमम्॥
en: On her by Rishis of royal descent three virtuous sons have been begotten; you too beget the fourth who will be the best among mankind.

sa: अदुष्टं वर्तमाने तु हृदयान्तरपूरुषे। तेनैव देवाः प्रीयन्ते सतां मार्गस्थितेन वै॥
en: When the Purusha that lives in one's heart is pure, and walks in the path of the righteous, the gods take a pleasure in him.

sa: ततश्चचाल पृथिवी सपर्वतवनद्रुमा। संतप्तानि च भूतानि विषादं जग्मुरुत्तमम्॥
en: Then the earth, with the mountains, forests and trees, began to tremble, and all creatures, becoming heated, became highly afflicted.

sa: रक्षांसि च पिशाचाश्च विनेदुरतिसङ्गताः। ववुश्चाशिशिरा वाताः सूर्यो नैव तताप च॥
en: The Rakshasa and the Pisachas, joining together to utter fierced yells; inauspicious winds began to blow and the Sun ceased to shine and give heat.

sa: द्रव्येषु समतीतेषु ये गुणास्तान् न चिन्तयेत्। न तानाद्रियमाणस्य स्नेहबन्धः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: When things are passed, one should not grieve, thinking of their merits. He who thinks of such past things with affection can never liberate himself.

sa: एवं सुयुद्धे पार्थेन जिताहं मधुसूदन। स्वयंवरे महत् कर्म कृत्वा न सुकरं परैः॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, I was thus obtained in the Saimvara by Partha (Arjuna) who performed a feat difficult of achievment by others and who fought with the assembled kings.

sa: एतादृशानि दुःखानि सहन्ती दुर्बलीयसाम्। दीर्घकालं प्रदीप्तास्मि पापानां पापकर्मणाम्॥
en: Suffering such wrongs at the hands of the sinful, evil-doing and weak foes, am I to suffer misery so long?

sa: संजय उवाच तत् प्रभग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा कुन्तीपुत्रो धनजयः। न्यवारयदमेयात्मा द्रोणपुत्रजयेप्सया॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding the troops broken and routed Kunti's son Dhananjaya of illustrious soul, rallied them from a desire of slaying the son of Drona.

sa: असितो देवलश्चैव तथा नारदपर्वतौ। कक्षीवान् जामदग्न्यश्च रामस्ताण्ड्यस्तथाऽऽत्मवान्।। वसिष्ठो जमदग्निश्च विश्वामित्रोऽत्रिरेव च। भरद्वाजो हरिश्मश्रुः कुण्डधारः श्रुतश्रवाः॥ एते महर्षयः स्तुत्वा विष्णुमृग्भिः समाहिताः। लेभिरे तपसा सिद्धिं प्रसादात् तस्य धीमतः॥
en: Then, again, Asita and Devala, and Narada and Paravata, and Kakshivat, and Jamadagni's son Rama, and Tandya possessed of purified soul, and Vashishtha, and Jamadagni, and Vishvamitra, and Atri, and Bharadvaja, and Harishmashru, and Kundadhara, and Shrutashravas,-these great Rishis, by worshipping Vishnu with concentrated minds with the help of Richs, and by penances, acquired success through the grace of that great god gifted with intelligence.

sa: दह्यमाने स्वके गेहे दग्धा इति ततो जनाः। न गर्हयेयुरस्मान् वै पाण्डवार्थाय कर्हिचित्॥
en: The people will think that they have been burnt to death in that burning house; and therefore none will be able to blame us for the death of the Pandavas,

sa: शकटानि रथाश्चैव तावदेव करेणवः। खराणां पुरुषाणां च परिसंख्या न विद्यते॥
en: Of cars there were as many, and of carts too as many and of she elephants as many. Mules and men were of unlimited number.

sa: समनुप्राप्तकृच्छोऽहं मोहं परममागतः। भीष्मद्रोणौ हतौ श्रुत्वा नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥
en: I am plunged in distress and a swoon overwhelms me. Oh, I cannot live hearing both Bhishma and Drona slain.

sa: यत्रेष्ट्वा भगवान् स्थाणुः पूजयित्वा सरस्वतीम्। स्थापयामास तत् तीर्थं स्थाणुतीर्थमिति प्रभो॥
en: Having performed a sacrifice there and adored the river Sarasvati, Sthanu established that tirtha there. Therefore it is known by the name Sthanu-tirtha, O lord.

sa: एक:समुद्धृतः पिण्डो ह्यधस्तात् कस्य गच्छति॥ कं वा प्रीणयते देवं कथं तारयते पितॄन।
en: Whom does that riceball which is thrown into the waters reach? How does it , by being so thrown please the deities, and how does it rescue the departed Manes?

sa: चातुर्वण्र्यं तथा वेदाश्चातुराश्रम्यमेव च। सर्वं प्रमुह्यते ह्येतद् यदा राजा प्रमाद्यति॥
en: The four castes, the Vedas, and the duties of the four modes of life, all suffer from confusion and weakness when the king becomes heedless.

sa: चाण्डालोऽहं ततो राजन् भुक्त्वा तदभवं नृप। ब्रह्मस्वहारी च नृपः सोऽप्रतिष्ठां गतिं ययौ।॥
en: Having taken that food, O Kshatriya, I have, in this life, become a Chandala. The king who had stolen the kine belonging to a Brahmana came by a wretched end.

sa: प्रविभागं तु पिण्डानां प्रवक्ष्याम्यनुपूर्वशः। पिण्डो ह्यधस्ताद् गच्छंस्तु अप आविश्य भावयेत्।।
en: We shall explain the classification of the riccballs offered at a Shraddha, The first ricehall should be thought of as being thrown into the waters.

sa: विश्वामित्रवसिष्ठौ तावहन्यहनि भारत। स्पर्धा तपःकृतां तीव्रां चक्रतुस्तौ तपोधनौ॥
en: The two ascetics Vishvamitra and Vashishtha, O Bharata, competed keenly with each other in respect of superiority of their penances.

sa: दृष्ट्वैव च स राजानं शंकरो लोकभावनः। उवाच परमप्रीतः श्वेतकिं नृपसत्तमम्॥
en: On seeing the king and being much pleased with him, the creator of the world Shankara (Shiva) spoke thus to that best of monarchs, Shvetaki.

sa: यत: प्रभृति संग्रामः कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः। ततः प्रभृति तां कन्यामपश्यन् द्रौणिमेव च॥
en: The Pandava soldiers dreamt that lady and Drona's son every night from the day when the battle between the Kurus and the Pandavas first began.

sa: ततः संग्रामभूमिं च वर्तमाने जनक्षये। अवेक्षमाणो गोविन्दः सव्यसाचिनामब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon, Govinda, after having observed the field of battle during the course of the slaughter of men, addressed Savyasachin, sayingएष

sa: तान् प्रभुः कृतमित्युक्त्वा सत्कृत्य च यथार्हतः। अभ्येत्य चैषां वेश्मानि पुनरायात् सहैव तैः॥
en: The Lord saving to them "you have done your part” and paying then due homage and coming to their houses, again came back to his own encampment with their company,

sa: तस्य तन्मतमाज्ञाय चक्रुरावसथं नराः। क्षणेन चान्नपानानि गुणवन्ति समार्जयन्॥
en: The men, knowing that intention of his in a moment, prepared a lodging; and collected together suitable food and drink.

sa: जगाम तदहश्चापि तेषां वर्षशतं यथा। निशां प्रतीक्षमाणानां दिदृक्षूणां मृतान् नृपान्॥
en: They passed that day as if it were a whole year, waiting for the approach of the might when they would see the deceased princes.

sa: तमः संवृतमप्यासीत् सर्वं जगदिदं तथा। न दिशो नादिशो राजन् प्रज्ञायन्ते स्म रेणुना॥
en: The whole of this world was enveloped with darkness; and neither the cardinal nor subsidiary points of the earth could be known on account of the dust that was raised.

sa: यस्यां यस्यामवस्थायां यद्यत् कर्म करोति यः। तस्यां तस्यामवस्थायां तत्फलं समवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Whatever actions are performed by a man under whatever circumstances, he gets the fruits of those those actions under whatever circumstances they may be performed.

sa: ततो वयं परिश्रान्ताः सततं कर्मवाहिनः। श्रमादस्मात् परिश्रान्तान् स त्वं नस्त्यक्तुमर्हसि॥ बुद्धिमोहं समास्थाय त्वरासम्भावितोऽनघ। गच्छ रुद्रसकाशं त्वं स हि त्वां याजयिष्यति॥
en: We have been fatigued by assisting you (at your sacrifices). We are tried in consequence of this labour; therefore, you should give us leave (to go away). O sinless one, from your loss of judgement only you cannot wait. Go to Rudra (Shiva); he will assist you at your sacrifice."

sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तेऽभिमुखा वीरा वासुदेवमुपास्थिताः। तेषां मध्ये महाबाहुः केशवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: When this was spoken, all the heroes turned their faces towards Vasudeva and the mighty armed Keshava (Krishna) thus spoke in their midst.

sa: न हि तत् कुरुते संख्ये रथी रिपुवधोद्यतः। यथा वै कुरुते कृष्ण सारथिर्यलमास्थितः॥
en: A car-warrior desirous of slaying his adversary cannot, in battle, do that (to achieve his purpose) which, O Krishna, his driver can do, if this latter strides with due caution.

sa: हारिद्रवर्णा ये त्वेते हेमपुङ्खाः शिलाशिताः। नकुलस्य कलापोऽयं पञ्चशार्दूललक्षणः॥
en: The quiver, having the five images of tigers full of yellow, gold winged shafts whetted on stone, belongs to Nakula.

sa: कच्चिद्धृदि न ते शोको राजन् पुत्रविनाशजः। कच्चिज्ज्ञानानि सर्वाणि सुप्रसन्नानि तेऽनघ॥
en: Has your grief begotten of the destruction of our sons in battle, disappeared from your heart? Are all your perceptions, O sinless one, now clear?

sa: अकार्यमपि येनेह प्रयुक्तः सेवते नरः। तं लोभमसिभिस्तीक्ष्णैनिकृत्य सुखमेधते॥
en: Urged by that fault, one induigcs in forbidden deeds. Do you cut off, cut off, that cupidity with sharp-edged swords.

sa: स सायकः कर्णभुजप्रमुक्तः शक्राशनिप्रख्यरुचिः शिताग्रः॥ भुजान्तरं प्राप्य धनंजयस्य विवेश वल्मीकमिवोरगोत्तमः।
en: The keen arrows, effulgent like Shakra's thunder-bolt shot off Karna's hands, fell upon Dhananjaya's breast and went into it like a serpent penetrating an ant-hill.

sa: उष्मतो म्लायते पण त्वक् फलं पुष्पमेव च। म्लायते शीर्यते चापि स्पर्शस्तेनात्र विद्यते॥
en: They have heat within them for which leaf, bark, fruit, and flower are seen to fall off. They sicken and dry up. This indicates that they have perception of touch.

sa: श्रुत्वा भवत्सकाशाद्धि पितुर्वृत्तमशेषतः। कल्याणं प्रतिपत्स्यामि विपरीतं न जातुचित्॥
en: Hearing from you all about my father, I shall do what is proper and good. I shall not do otherwise.

sa: तस्य चिन्तापरीतस्य बुद्धिर्जज्ञे महात्मनः॥ बहुव्यालमृगाकीर्णं त्यक्तुं द्वैतवनं वनम्।
en: That high-souled hero, filled with anxiety, made up his mind to abandon the forest of Dvaitavana abounding in wild animals.

sa: स्वर्गं ह्येव समास्थाय रणयज्ञेषु दीक्षिताः। जयन्ति क्षत्रिया लोकांस्तद् विद्धि मनुजर्षभ॥
en: O best of men, know that Kshatriyas, being installed in the sacrifice of war with the view of heaven before them, conquer the whole world.

sa: एष न्द्रिो वैजयन्तो गुणैर्नित्यं समाहितः। येनासुरान् पराजित्य जगत् पाति शतक्रतुः॥
en: It is graced with many merits; it is through this, Shatakratu (Indra) has became what he is; he rules the universe by vanquishing the Asuras.

sa: पिता नस्त्वं गुरुर्बन्धुस्तथा पुत्रास्तु ते वयम्। इति मन्यामहे सर्वे भवन्तं प्रणता स्थिताः॥
en: But, O Drona, I am no lament Arjuna. I am Bhimasena your enemy. We used to regard you as our father, preceptor and friend and we were like your sons.

sa: एतत् पार्थमनुप्राप्तं वरुणाच्चारुदर्शनम्॥ पूजितं सुरमत्र्येषु बिभर्ति परमं वपुः।
en: This beautiful bow has come to Partha from Varuna. Worshipped by god and men it has taken a handsome form.

sa: एवं व्यवसिते लोके बहुदोषे युधिष्ठिर। आत्ममोक्षनिमित्तं वै यतेत मतिमान् नरः॥
en: When the world, O Yudhishthira, which is full of shortcomings, is so framed, every intelligent man, should try to acquire the liberation of his soul.

sa: तथा नष्टं तमो घोरं दीपैर्दीप्तरितस्ततः। द्योश्चैव पृथिवी चापि दिशश्च प्रदिशस्तथा॥
en: So that pitchy darkness pervading the field of battle was destroyed by those blazing lamps. The firmament, the earth, the cardinal and the minor points.

sa: देवयान्युवाच वेदाहं तात बालापि धर्माणां यदिहान्तरम्। अक्रोधे चातिवादे च वेद चापि बलाबलम्॥
en: the power Devayani said: O father, I know, though I am a girl, what are duties and virtues. I also know the difference between anger and forgiveness and of each.

sa: ततः स विप्रस्तां नागी समाधाय पुनः पुनः। तदेव पुलिनं नद्याः प्रययौ ब्राह्मणर्षभः॥
en: Having said this repeatedly to the wife of the Naga, the foremost of Brahmanas went to the banks of the Gomati for living there till the time of Naga's return.

sa: न हि दुःखेषु शोचन्ते न प्रहृष्यन्ति चर्धिषु। कृतप्रज्ञा ज्ञानतृप्ताः क्षान्ताः सन्तो मनीषिणः॥
en: They who acquired wisdom, and have won contentment therefrom, they who are of tranquil should, who are virtuous and good among creatures, never grieve in misery nor rejoice in happiness.

sa: कथं सृष्टानि भूतानि कथं वर्णविभक्तयः। शौचशौचं कथं तेषां धर्माधर्मविधिः कथम्॥
en: How were all objects created? Whence has this division of creatures originated? Whence are their purity and impurity, and the laws about virtue and vice?

sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः पाण्डवेयेन महात्मा ऋषिसंनिधौ। उवाच भगवांस्तत्र मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by the illustrious Pandava in the midst of the Rishis, the exalted and the greatly ascetic Markandeya said-

sa: इन्द्र उवाच किमिष्यते धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठ यद् द्रष्टुकामोऽसि तमप्रमेयम्। अनन्तमायामितमन्त्रवीर्य नारायणं ह्यादिदेवं पुराणम्॥
en: Indra said What is your object, О foremost of virtuous persons, in thus trying to see that Ancient and First of gods, viz., Narayana, of inconceivable power, and numberless illusions.

sa: दक्षिणेन सरस्वत्याः स्वयनं तीर्थमुत्तमम्॥ तस्मिन् देशे त्वनिरिणे ते तु युद्धमरोचयन्।
en: That was an excellent Tirtha on the southern side of the Sarasvati. The ground there was not sandy, and was therefore, selected for the battle.

sa: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि धर्ममर्थविनिश्चयम्। निर्मर्यादे वर्तमाने दानवैकार्णवे पुरा॥ बभूव राजा राजेन्द्र मान्धाता नाम वीर्यवान्। पुरा वसुमतीपालो यज्ञं चक्रे दिदृक्षया॥ अनादिमध्यनिधनं देवं नारायणं प्रभुम्। स राजा राजशार्दूल मान्धाता परमेश्वरम्॥
en: I shall now recite to you a history consisting of the conclusions of both religion and profit. In days of yore when the Danavas had multiplied and done away with all impediments and distinctions, the powerful Mandhatri, O monarch, became king. That lord of the Earth, viz., king Mandhatri, celebrated a great sacrifice with a view to see the powerful Narayana, that god of gods, without beginning, middle, and end.

sa: स समेत्य महेन्द्राण्या देवराजः शतक्रतुः। मुदा परमया युक्तः पालयामास देवराट्॥
en: Being united with his queen the great Indra, the king of the gods, the performer of a hundred sacrifices, highly pleased ruled over the gods.

sa: कीदृशो जीवतां जीवः क्व वा गच्छन्ति ये मृताः। परलोकमिमं चापि सर्वं शंसितुमर्हसि॥
en: What type of individual soul is of the living creatures? Where they go after the death. What is this and next world? You are able to explain all the things.

sa: एष भीमो महाक्रोधी हीनः पाण्डवसृञ्जयैः। मदीयैरावृतो योधैः कर्ण नन्दयतीव माम्॥
en: O Karna, there the highly enraged Bhimia, forsaken by the Pandavas and the Srinjayas and surrounded by my own warriors, affords great joy to me.

sa: तमेनमनुवर्तन्ते सात्यकिप्रमुखा रथाः। पञ्चालाः केकया मत्स्याः पाण्डवाश्च विशेषतः॥
en: Car-warriors headed by Satyaki and the Panchalas, the Kekayas, the Matsyas and specially the Pandavas, are following him (in battle).

sa: तस्य पौरवकालिङ्गौ काम्बोजश्च सुदक्षिणः॥ क्षेमधन्वा च शल्यश्च तस्थुः प्रमुखतो रथाः।
en: Paurava, the ruler of Kalingas, Sudakshina, the ruler of the Kombojas, Kshemadhanvan, and Sumitra, those great car-warriors took up their positions in front of Duryodhana.

sa: शुशुभे केतुमुख्येन पावकेन कलिङ्गकः। श्वेतच्छत्रेण निष्केण चामरव्यजनेन च॥
en: The king of the Kalingas with his high firelike effulgent standard, with his white umbrella and Chamaras looked exceedingly beautiful.

sa: संजय उवाच धार्तराष्ट्राण्यनीकानि दृष्ट्वा व्यूढानि पाण्डवः। अभ्यभाषत धर्मात्मा धर्मराजो धनंजयम्॥
en: Sanjaya said seeing the troops of the Kurus placed in battle-array, the virtuous minded son of Pandu, Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, thus spoke spoke to Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

sa: अशोभत मुखे तस्य भीमसेनो महाबलः। नेत्रे शिखण्डी दुर्धर्षो धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥
en: And in the backs of that hawk-like array shone Bhimasena possessed of great strength. In its eyes Shikhandin and the irrepressible Dhrishtadyumna the of Prishata.

sa: उत्थितेषु कबन्धेषु सर्वतः शोणितोदके। समरे पर्यधावन्त नृपा रिपुवधोद्यताः॥
en: As head-less trunks stood up in that sea of blood, other kings rushed into battle endeavoring to slay their enemies.

sa: तस्य शक्तिं महावेगां भीमसेनो महाबलः। क्रुद्धाशीविषसंकाशां प्रेषयामास भारत॥
en: Thereat the mighty Bhimasena hurled at Bhishma, O Bharata his lance charged with fierce momentum and resembling an enraged snake.

sa: युध्यमानान् यथाशक्ति घटमानाञ्जयं प्रति। पाण्डवा हि जयन्त्येव जीयन्ते चैव मामकाः॥
en: Yough they are fighting to the best of their powers, and striving hard to secure victory over them, whilst they are becoming reduced in number.

sa: विविंशतिः पञ्चभिश्च त्रिभिर्दुःशासनस्तथा। तान् प्रत्यविध्यद् राजेन्द्र पार्षतः शत्रुतापनः॥
en: Vivingshati with five, and Dushasana with three. Them, O monarch, the son of Prishata, the slayer of his foes, pierced.

sa: परिवत्रुस्तदा पार्थं सहपुत्रं महारथम्॥ एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु सूर्येऽस्तमुपगच्छति।
en: Surrounded the mighty car-warrior Arjuna along with his son. At that moment the sun having gone down below the horizon.

sa: स गजान् गदया निघ्नन् व्यचरत् समरे बली। भीमसेनो महाबाहुः सवज्र इव वासवः॥
en: Then like the slayer of Vritra moving amidst the Danava host, the mighty armed Bhimasena, endued with great strength, careered on the filed of battle, slaughtering elephants with his mace.

sa: ततः शैक्यायसीं गुर्वी प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्। अधावत् तावकान् योधान् दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः॥
en: Thereafter taking up his huge and heavy mace made of Shaikya iron, he (Bhimasena) rushed against your warriors, like the Destroyer himself wielding his club.

sa: द्वादशैव तु वर्षाणि वने धिष्ण्याद् विवासितः। संवत्सरं विराटस्य दास्यमास्थाय चोषितः॥
en: For twelve years have you been exiled from your home into the woods, and for a whole year you lived as a slave under Virata.

sa: रलम्बुषो राक्षसोऽसौ तदानीम्। शरैश्चतुर्भिः प्रतिविद्ध्य तं च नप्ता शिनेरभ्यपतद् रथेन॥
en: Then the Rakshasa Alambhusa pierced him with ten shafts only. Piercing him in return with fine arrows, the grandson of Shini, advanced on his car.

sa: यत् तु मे कथितं तात मुनिभिर्भावितात्मभिः। पुराणगीतं धर्मज्ञ तच्छृणुष्व यथातथम्॥
en: Hear from me, you who are versed in morality, the ancient history that was related to me, O sire, by the sages of tranquil souls.

sa: मौर्वी ध्वजं धनुश्चेव युगमीषां तथैव च। रथिनां कुट्टयामास भल्लैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: With his bhallas of straight knots Arjuna then began to sever the bowstrings, the standards, the bows, the yokes and the shafts of many car-warriors.

sa: न वै विभीषिकां कांचिद् राजन् कुर्वन्ति पाण्डवाः। युध्यन्ति ते यथान्यायं शक्तिमन्तश्च संयुगे॥
en: Neither, O monarch, did the sons of Pandu create any new source of apprehension. Those warriors endued with strength are fighting their battles according to the rules of fair combat.

sa: भीष्मस्य तद् वचः श्रुत्वा सर्व एव महारथाः। द्रोणभीष्मौ पुरस्कृत्य भगदत्तपरीप्सया॥
en: Listening to those words of Bhishma all the monarchs forming in serried files and headed by the son Bharadvaja, with a desire for rescuing Bhagadatta.

sa: अनिलो वा वहेन्मेरुं द्यौर्वापि निपतेन्महीम्। युगं वा परिवर्तेन यद्येवं स्याद् यथाऽऽत्य माम्॥
en: But even the wind may move the Meru mountain, the heaven may fall over the earth, the periods now reigning may change, if what you have told me ever happens.

sa: अनुमानेन संज्ञाभिर्नामगोत्रैश्च संयुगे। वर्तते च तथा युद्धं तत्र तत्र विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, everywhere the battle raged the combatants were guided only by the indications afforded by colours, by watchwords, by names and by tribal distinctions.

sa: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ काम्बोजाश्च शकैः सह। पुच्छमासन् महाराज शूरसेनाश्च सर्वशः॥
en: O great king, Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, the Kambojas with the Shakas and also the Shurasenas formed its tail.

sa: सात्यकिश्चापि संक्रुद्धौ राक्षसं क्रूरमाहवे। अलम्बुषं शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्विव्याध बलिना वरः॥
en: Then Satyaki, inflamed with wrath in that conflict, covered, on all sides, the ruthless Rakshasas Alambusha, with his dreadful arrows.

sa: रथे यश्च गजेभ्यश्च हयेभ्यश्च नराधिपाः। पतिताः पात्यमानाश्च दृश्यन्तेऽर्जुनसायकैः॥
en: Kings were seen falling from their cars; elephants and horses were also seen to fall cut down by Arjuna's arrows.

sa: पश्चार्धे तस्य पद्मस्तु गर्भव्यूहः सुदुर्भिदः। सूची पद्मस्य गर्भस्थो गूढो व्यूहः कृतः पुनः॥
en: In the back portion of that array was formed another impenetrable array figuring a lotus. Within this latter again was constructed another closely formed array, that was designated the needle.

sa: हयांश्च चतुरः शीघ्रं निजघान महाबलः। शरैश्चैनं सुनिशितैः क्षिप्रं विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: Also that mighty car-warrior slew the four steeds of the latter in battle, and quickly pierced his person with seven shafts of exceeding sharpness. arrows

sa: तद् विहाय धनुश्छिन्नं सौभद्रः परवीरहा। अन्यदादत्तवांश्चित्रं कार्मुकं वेगवत्तरम्॥
en: Then that slayer of hostile heroes, Subhadara's son, throwing aside the broken bow, took up another beautiful and tough bow.

sa: तत् तं विलपितं सर्वं मया राजन् निशामितम्। अर्थे निविशमानस्य विषमिश्रं यथा मधु॥
en: Therefore, O king, all these lamentations of yours that I have heard, you who are absorbed in the enjoyment of worldly objects-appear to me to be like honey-mixed with poison.

sa: चेकितानस्ततः खङ्गं क्रोधादुद्धृत्य भारत। लाघवं परमास्थाय गौतमं समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thereupon Chekitana, O Bharata, drawing his sword out of its sheath, with admirable activity rushed at the son of Gautami.

sa: नियुज्यमानाः स्थास्यन्ति पाण्डवा धर्मवर्मनि। सन्ति मे ज्ञातयस्तात येषां श्रोष्यन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: Obtaining sovereignty they will ever remain in the path of virtue. I have kinsmen, O son, to whose words the Pandavas will ever pay attention.

sa: सोऽपश्यच्च कलिङ्गेषु चरन्तमरिसूदनः । भीमसेनं महाबाहुं पार्षतः परवीरहा॥
en: That slayer of hostile heroes, the Prishata prince saw that chastiser of foes the mightyarmed Bhimasena fighting among the Kalingas.

sa: विविंशतेर्तुर्मुखस्य चित्रसेनविकर्णयोः। अन्येषां च सुतानां मे न तथा श्रूयते ध्वनिः॥
en: I do not now hear those sounds I used to hear formerly in the camps of Vivinshati, Durmukha, Chitrasena, Vikarna and other sons of mine.

sa: प्रेक्षस्व भीष्मं युधि भीमवेगं सर्वांस्तपन्त मम सैन्यसंघान्। शरौघजालैरतितिग्मवेगैः कालं यथा कालकृतं क्षणेन॥
en: Behold Bhishma of tremendous impetuosity falling upon my host of troops destroying it with a shower of arrows of excessive effulgence, like the Destroyer himself destroying everything in a moment,

sa: निकृत्तचापः समरेऽनपेक्षः पराजितः शान्तनवेन चाजौ। विहाय बन्धूनथ सोदरांश्च क्व यास्यसे नानुरूपं तवेदम्॥
en: Having your bow severed, shunning the fight, vanquished by the royal son of Shantanu, whither are you going forsaking your friends and your uterine brothers? this does not befit you.

sa: निवेशने सत्यधृतेः सोमदत्तस्य संजय। आसीनोऽहं पुरा तात शब्दमश्रौषमुत्तमम्॥
en: Formerly, O Sanjaya, while sitting in the camp of the truth-loving Somadatta, I used to hear all those charming sounds.

sa: संनिवार्य स तां घोरां शरवृष्टिं समुत्थिताम्। गदामादाय तरसा संनिपत्य महाबलः॥
en: Resisting that shower of arrows, that great warrior (Bhima) then took up his fearful mace. He then jumped down from his car in great speed.

sa: तत्र दुर्योधनो राजा निवेश्य बलमोजसा। सम्मानयित्वा नृपतीन् यस्य गुल्मांस्तथैव च॥
en: The king Duryodhana, having encamped his soldiers there strongly, and having paid his respects to the rulers of men on his side and posted guards,

sa: स त्वमद्य महाबाहो राजानां परिपालय। यथैव हि मया गुप्तस्त्वया गुप्तो भवेत् तथा॥
en: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, do you protect the king this day. So that, protected by you he will be as safe as if he were protected by my own self.

sa: ततो युधिष्ठिरो वश्यान् राज्ञस्तान् समचोदयत्। भीष्मं शान्तनवं सर्वे निहतेति सुहृद्गणान्॥
en: Thereafter, O king, Yudhishthira urged the kings on his side and his relatives, saying "Uniting together do you all slay Bhishma the son of Shantanu."

sa: मुहूर्तादिव तत् सर्वमभवत् स्वर्गसंनिभम्। न हि युद्धकथां कांचित् तत्राकुर्वन् महारथाः॥
en: For a short while only did that scene resemble paradise itself, and those foremost of mortals for a while desisted from talking of the battle.

sa: अथेत्युक्त्वा तु तौ वीरौ सर्वपारिषदैः सह। प्रस्थितौ तत्सरो दिव्यं दिव्यैश्वर्यशतैर्युतम्॥
en: Thereupon saying 'year to the words of Siva, the two heroes with all their followers, went to that celestial lake possessed hundreds of celestial wonders.

sa: ततः स पार्षतः क्रूरो व्यूह चक्रे सुदारुणम्। शृङ्गाटकं महाराज परव्यूहविनाशनम्॥
en: Thereupon, O mighty monarch, the valiant son of Prishata formed the dreadful array known as Shringataka that is capable of penetrating through the hostile array.

sa: द्वादशैव तु वर्षाणि वने धिष्ण्याद् विवासितः। संवत्सरं विराटस्य दास्यमास्थाय चोषितः॥
en: For twelve years have you been exiled from your home into the woods, and for a whole year you lived as a slave under Virata.

sa: योधयामास कालिङ्गं स्वबाहुबलमाश्रितः। शक्रदेवस्तु समरे विसृजन् सायकान् बहून्॥
en: Fought with the Kalinga king, depending only on his own prowess of arms. Shakradeva shot innumerable arrows in that battle.

sa: गजो गवाक्षो वृषभश्चर्मवानार्जवः शुकः। षडेते बलसम्पन्ना निर्ययुर्महतो बलात्॥
en: Gaja, Gavaksha, Vrishabha, Charmavan, Arjava and Shuka, these six highly puissant heroes rode out of the mighty ranks the Kauravas,

sa: पुरतोऽपि च पृष्ठे च पार्श्वयोश्च भृशाहतः। एको बहुभिरत्यर्थं धैर्याद् राजन् न विव्यथे॥
en: Single-handed as he was, he was smitten sore by many, on his chest, his back, and his flanks; but o king he flinched not in consequence of his great patience.

sa: विकृष्य च शितं खङ्गं गृहीत्वा च शरावरम्। पदातिर्दृतमागच्छज्जिघांसुः सौबलान् युधि॥
en: Then drawing his sharp saber and holding his buckler, he (Iravat) quickly ran on foot desirous of slaying the sons of Subala, in that battle.

sa: एते चान्ये च बहवो नानाजनपदेश्वराः। समेताः पाण्डवस्यार्थं वासुदेवपुरोगमाः॥
en: These and many other lords of cities have been united together for the sake of the Pandavas headed by Vasudeva.

sa: मुमोच निशितान् बाणान् राक्षसेषु परंतप। जघान् च महेष्वासः प्रधानांस्तत्र राक्षसान्॥
en: That highly powerful hero sped arrows of exceeding sharpness at those Rakshasas, and that fierce bowman slew many of the Rakshasas that were fighting there.

sa: श्रुतः। सर्वांस्त्वन्यान् हनिष्यामि पार्थावान् भरतर्षभ यान् समेष्यामि समरे न तु कुन्तीसुतान् नृप॥
en: all other rulers of the earth, I shall slay, O foremost among the Bharatas, those whom I meet in battle, but not the son of Kunti, O ruler of men.

sa: इति स्म वाचोऽश्रूयन्त प्रोच्चरन्त्यस्ततस्ततः। गाङ्गेयार्जुनयोः संख्ये स्तवयुक्ता विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, we heard these words full of praise of both the son of Ganga and the son of Pritha.

sa: मयाभिषिक्तो राजेन्द्र यवीयानपि धर्मतः। विचित्रवीर्यो धर्मात्मा मामेव समुदैक्षत॥
en: Installed by me, O chief among kings, my younger brother the virtuous souled Vichitravirya looked up to me in everything.

sa: नरा नरान् समासाद्य क्रोधरक्तेक्षणा भृशम्। उरांस्युरोभिरन्योन्यं समाश्लिष्य निजनिरे॥
en: Combatants, with eyes crimsoned in rage, meeting one another, struck one another with their breasts, and thus killed one another.

sa: ततस्ते मां महीपाला: सर्व एवं विशाम्पते। रथवातेन महता सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Then did all those rulers of the earth, O lord of the universe, surround me on an all sides with a large troupe of chariots.

sa: शरवेगसमुत्कृत्तै राज्ञां केशव मूर्धभिः। आस्तीर्यमाणां पृथिवीं द्रष्टासि श्वो मया युधि॥
en: Tomorrow you shall see the earth covered by me with the head of princes cut-off their trunks by the force of my arrows, O Keshava.

sa: पक्षौ तु भीमसेनश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥ द्रौपदेयाभिमन्युश्च सात्यकिश्च महारथः।
en: Bhimasena, the descendant of Prishat Dhrishtadyumna, the sons of Draupadi, Abhimanyu, and that great car-warrior Satyaki became its two wings.

sa: स्पर्धते हि महेष्वासो नित्यं द्रोणसुतेन सः। स विस्फार्य महच्चापं द्रौणिं विव्याध पत्रिणा॥
en: That fierce bowmen (Nila) ever longed for an encounter with the son of Drona. Now stretching his mighty bow he pierced with many a winged shaft the son of Drona,

sa: दने नीलविनाशाय मति मतिमतां वरः। ततः संधाय विमलान् भल्लान् कर्मारमार्जितान्॥
en: That foremost of intelligent heroes resolved to slay Nila in battle. Thereafter fixing on the bowstring broaded-headed shafts, resplendent and variegated by the forger himself,

sa: तथेतरे चाभ्यधावन् राक्षसा युद्धदुर्मदाः। तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसं घोरदर्शनम्॥
en: Other inferior Rakshasas invincible in battle also rushed to the fight. Seeing that Rakshasa of dreadful aspect make towards himself,

sa: बन्धुभिर्विप्रहीणास्मि शाल्वेन च निराकृता। न च शक्यं पुनर्गन्तुं मया वारणसाह्वयम्॥
en: I have been robbed of my friends and wronged by Shalva nor am I capable of going back to the city called after the elephant.

sa: राक्षसापसदं हन्तु स्वयमेव पितामह। त्वां समाश्रित्य दुर्धर्षं तन्मे कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि॥
en: O grandsire, to slay that worst of Rakshasas myself, mainly depending upon your invincible self. It behaves you to see that my wish is fulfilled.”

sa: कृष्ण भीष्मः सुसंरब्धः सहितः सर्वपार्थिवैः। क्षपयिष्यति नो नूनं यादृशोऽस्य पराक्रमः॥
en: OKrishna, such is the prowess of Bhishma; if he is angry, he will, with the help of the kings (on his side), certainly annihilate us.

sa: वारयामास तान् द्रोणो जलौघमचलो यथा। पाण्डवान् समरे क्रुद्धान् पाञ्चालांश्च सकेकयान्॥
en: Then like unto a mountain checking the progress of torrents of water, in that battle, Drona held in check the enraged Pandavas, Parichalas and Kekayas.

sa: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय कृतवर्मा महारथः। पञ्चभिः सायकैस्तूर्णं विव्याधोरसि भारत॥
en: Thereat, O Bharata, the mighty car-warrior Kritavarman taking up another bow quickly pierced Arjuna on the chest with five arrows.

sa: एवं गते तु किं भद्रे शक्यं कर्तुं तपस्विभिः। आश्रमस्थैर्महाभागे तपोयुक्तर्महात्मभिः॥
en: Such being the case, gentle lady, what can be done by devotees residing in this hermitage, of great parts and great souled though they be?

sa: सा त्वेनमब्रवीद् राजन् क्रियतां मदनुग्रहः। प्राव्राज्यमहमिच्छामि तपस्तप्स्यामि दुश्चरम्॥
en: She however thus replied, O king: "Show me this favour. I desire to wander about and to practice hard devotion.

sa: वधो नूनं प्रतिज्ञातो मम गाण्डीवधन्वना। तथा हि हृष्टाः क्रोशन्ति शोककाले स्म पाण्डवाः॥
en: Without doubt, the wielder of the bow Gandiva has promised to slay me; therefore it is that, the Pandavas are shouting with delight at a time when they should grieve.

sa: स तामाश्वासयत् कन्यां दृष्टान्तागमहेतुभिः। सान्त्वयामास कार्यं च प्रतिजज्ञे द्विजैः सह॥
en: He then comforted that lady by citing instances and examples and consoled her by promising to do her work along with others among the twice-born.

sa: शक्यो जेतुं यमः क्रुद्धो वज्रपाणिश्च संयुगे। वरुणः पाशभृद् वापि कुबेरो वा गदाधरः॥
en: Even angry Yama himself, or the wielder of the thunder-bolt (Indra) or the wielder of the noose, Varuna, or the holder of the mace, Kubera, may be defeated in battle.

sa: आश्रमे वै वसन्त्यास्ते न भवेयुः पितुर्गुहे। ततस्त्वन्येऽब्रुवन् वाक्यं तापसास्तां तपस्विनीम्॥
en: In a life in the hermitage while there will be none in your father's place. Then did other anchorites say to that female devotee these

sa: द्रोणस्तु समरे वीरं निर्दहन्तं सुतांस्तव। यथाद्रिं वारिधाराभिः समन्ताद् व्यकिरच्छरैः। :॥
en: Then Drona covered that hero (Bhima) who had been consuming your sons, with a shower of shafts, like showers of rain covering the mountain breast.

sa: गाङ्गेयो भगदत्तश्च गौतमश्च महारथाः। पाण्डवं रभसं युद्धे वारयामासुरर्जुनम्॥
en: The son of Ganga, Bhagadatta, the mighty car-warrior Gautami's son, all opposed in battle Arjuna himself the son of Pandu.

sa: स वेपमान उत्थाय मातुस्तस्याः तां कन्यामङ्कमारोप्य पर्यश्वासयत् प्रभो॥
en: The father of her mother then rose trembling (with rage) and placing her on his lap began to comfort her.

sa: आत्मानमेव गहेयं यदहं वै सुदुर्बलान्। युष्मानाज्ञाय निर्यातो भीरूनकृतनिश्चयान्॥
en: It is better I should blame myself, since knowing you all to be cowards, sneaking and irresolute, I went away.

sa: रणे चारूणि चापानि हेमपृष्ठानि मारिष। हतानामपविद्धानि कलापाश्च महाधनाः॥
en: Beautiful bows with their staves decked with gold, O Bharata, loosened from the hold of slain warriors, and precious ornaments,

sa: नानाविधानि शस्त्राणि प्रगृह्य पतिता नराः। जीवन्त इव दृश्यन्ते गतसत्त्वा महारथाः॥
en: Men lying on the field with diverse weapons in grasp looked as if alive, though those mighty car-warriors were all deprived of the vital breaths.

sa: विप्रविद्धैः कलापैश्च पतितैश्च शरासनैः। विप्रकीर्णैः शरैश्चैव रुक्मपुखैः समन्ततः॥
en: With ornaments of various kinds loosened from their places, with bows fallen about, with shafts of golden wings lying about,

sa: रथैश्च सर्वतो भग्नैः किङ्किणीजालभूषितैः। वाजिभिश्च हतैर्बाणैः स्रस्तजिह्वः सशोणितैः॥
en: With many broken cars decked with rows of bells, with numerous slain steeds bespattered with gore and their tongues protruding,

sa: तेन विद्राव्यमाणानि तव सैन्यानि संयुगे। चक्रुरास्विनं घोरं पर्जन्यनिनदोपमम्॥
en: Crushed by him, your troops in that battle, uttered terrible cries of distress resembling the rumbling of the rain clouds.

sa: संजय उवाच तस्मिन्नहनि निर्वृत्ते घोरे प्राणभृतां क्षये। आदित्येऽस्तं गते श्रीमान् संध्याकाल उपस्थिते॥
en: Sanjaya said When that dreadful day so fraught with the slaughter of creatures had passed away and when the sun set, the auspicious shade of twilight began to spread itself.

sa: कैकेयो धृष्टकेतुश्च अभिमन्युश्च वीर्यवान्। एतानापततः सर्वान् द्रोणशल्यकृपैः सह॥
en: The Kaikeya brothers, Dhrishtaketu and the greatly powerful Abhimanyu. Seeing them coming to his rescue, with Drona, Shalya, and Kripa.

sa: भीष्मं समभिदुद्राव जलौघ इव पर्वतम्। तस्य वेगमसंवार्यं मत्वा भीष्मः प्रतापवान्॥
en: He rushed upon Bhishma as a swollen river rushes upon a rock. Considering his great impetuosity as incapable of being checked, the greatly fearful Bhishma.

sa: भीष्म उवाच तमहं स्मयन्निव रणे प्रत्यभाष व्यवस्थितम्। भूमिष्ठं नोत्सहे योद्धं भवन्तं रथमास्थितः॥
en: Bhishma said Laughingly I said to him who stood there for battle: Myself riding on a chariot I do not venture to fight with you who are on the ground.

sa: ते तस्य विविशुस्तूर्णं कायं निर्भिद्य मर्मसु। त तैर्विभिन्नसर्वाङ्गः शुशुभे राक्षसोत्तमः॥
en: Those shafts, then piercing through his body, penetrated into his very vitals. His body mangled with those shafts, the foremost of the Rakshasas appeared beautiful,

sa: आर्जुनिः समरे सैन्यं तावकं सम्ममर्द ह। मदान्धो गन्धनागेन्द्रं सपद्मां पद्मिनीमिव॥
en: Then son of Arjuna began to crush your troops in battle like an infuriated excellent elephant agitating a lake having lotuses blooming in its waters.

sa: यः स्माद्यमनुपर्येति भूमिं कुर्वन्निमां सुखाम्। न चासीद् विक्रिया यस्यप्राप्य श्रियमनुत्तमाम्॥
en: Making this Earth abound in all kinds of happiness, he caused the primeval Yuga to set in. He was not perverted, having obtained cxcellent affluence.

sa: तस्याहं निशितं मल्लं चिक्षेप भरतर्षभ। तेनास्य धनुषः कोटि छित्त्वा भूमावपातयम्॥
en: Then did I hurl towards him a broad headed arrow and by it his bow broke into a million pieces and fell to the ground.

sa: तथैव पाण्डवा राजन् परिवार्य धनंजयम्। रणाय महते युक्ता दंशिता भरतर्षभ॥
en: So also, O king, the Pandavas, clad in mail, surrounding Dhananjaya, O foremost of the Bharatas, began to put forth all their energies in battle.

sa: ततोऽहमस्त्रं वायव्यं जामदग्न्ये प्रयुक्तवान्। प्रत्याजघ्ने च तद् रामो गुह्यकास्त्रेण भारत॥
en: Then did I shoot at the son of Jamadagni the weapons called Vayavya but Rama, O Bharata, warded if off by the weapon called Guhyaka.

sa: मेघजालस्य महतो यथा मध्यगतो रविः। व्यधमत् स गजानीकं गदया पाण्डवर्षभः॥
en: Like the sun shining in the midst of a mass of clouds. Then that foremost of the Pandavas, began to agitate that division of elephants,

sa: अपरे तु तदाऽऽदाय वाजिनागरथान् रणे। त्वरया परया युक्ताः प्राद्रवन्त विशाम्पते॥
en: Others, on the other hand, seizing steeds, elephants and chariots in that battle, fled away, O ruler of men, at the top of their speed.

sa: ततः पुनः शरं दीप्तं सुप्रभं कालसम्मितम्। असृजं जामदग्न्याय रामायाहं जिघांसया॥
en: Then did I shoot at Rama, the son of Jamadgna with the desire of killing him, blazing arrows of good appearance, guided by death itself.

sa: मद्रराजोऽपि तान् सर्वानाजघान त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः। युधिष्ठिरं पुनः षष्ट्या विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: The king of the Madras in return pierced them all with three shafts each; then again he pierced Yudhishthira with sixty shafts of exceeding sharpness;

sa: तस्मिन् हते महेष्वासे राजपुत्रे महारथे। हाहाकारो महानासीत् तव सैन्यस्य मारिष॥
en: Then, O Sire, when that mighty car-warrior and fierce bowman, that prince, was slain, loud cries of "Oh" and "Alas” war heard in your army.

sa: तां तु गाथां जगुः प्रीता गन्धर्वाः सूर्यवर्चसः। पितृदेवमनुष्याणां शृण्वतां बल्गुवादिनः॥
en: Gandharvas of melodious voice and solar effulgence, greatly pleased, sang this song in the hearing of the anscertral manes, the celestials and the human beings.

sa: नानावर्णविचित्राणि धनूंषि च महात्मनाम्। विस्फारितानि दृश्यन्ते तोयदेष्विव विद्युतः॥
en: The stretched bow of these illustrious warriors, decorated with various colours, looked like the flashes of lightning in the clouds.

sa: उत्तरं वै हतं दृष्ट्वा वैराटिर्भ्रातरं तदा। कृतवर्मणा च सहितं दृष्ट्वा शल्यमवस्थितम्॥ श्वेतः क्रोधात् प्रजज्वाल हविषा हव्यवाडिव। स विस्फार्य महच्चापं शक्रचापोपमं बली॥ अभ्यधावज्जिघांसन् वै शल्य मद्राधिपं बली। महता रथवंशेन समन्तात् परिवारितः॥ मुञ्चन् बाणमयं वर्ष प्रायाच्छल्यरधं प्रति। तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य मत्तवारणविक्रमम्॥ तावकानां रथाः सप्त समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्। मद्रराजमभीप्सन्तो मृत्योर्दष्ट्रान्तरं गतम्॥
en: Seeing his brother Uttara killed and seeing Shalya on the Kritavarman's car, Virata's son Shveta blazed up in anger as fire blazed forth with Ghee. That great warrior stretching his large bow that looked like that of Indra, rushed upon Shalya, the king of Madra with the desire of killing him. Surrounded on all sides with innumerable car-warriors, he advanced towards Shalya's chariot and poured upon him a on car shower of arrows. Seeing him rush to the fight with the prowess of an infuriated elephants, seven car-warriors of your side surrounded him on all sides with the desire of protecting the ruler of Madra who seemed to be already within the jaws of death.

sa: नाप्सु प्राणभृतां मृत्यु काले ज्वलनोऽदहत्। अधर्मरुचयो लुब्धा मूर्खा वा नाभवंस्तदा॥
en: Living creatures died not being drowned and prematurely; fire did not consume anything then. Then there were none, of vicious propensities and covetous and ignorant.

sa: भीष्योऽपि समरे जित्वा पाण्डवान् सहसृजयान्। पूज्यमानस्तव सुतैर्वन्द्यमानश्च भारत॥
en: Having vanquished the Pandavas and the Srinjayas in battle and adored and honoured by your sons, Bhishma then, O monarch.

sa: शिखण्डिनं समासाद्य भरतानां पितामहः। अवर्जयत संग्रामं स्त्रीत्वं तस्यानुसंस्मरन्।॥
en: But the grandsire of the Bharatas, meeting with Shikhandin in the battle avoided him, remembering the femininity of his sex.

sa: न चैवैनं महात्मानमुत्सहामो निरीक्षितुम्। लेलिह्यमानं सैन्येषु प्रवृद्धमिव पावकम्॥
en: We dare not even look at that illustrious warrior when he licks, like a raging conflagration, all my troops up.

sa: यथा घोरो महानागस्तक्षको वै विषोल्बणः। तथा भीष्मो रणे क्रुद्धस्तीक्ष्णशस्त्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: The mighty puissant Bhishma, possessed of sharp weapons and inflamed with rage battle, appears like the mighty snake Takshaka of great ferocity and virulent venom.

sa: गृहीतचापः समरे प्रमुञ्चन् निशिताञ्छरान्। शक्यो जेतुं यमः क्रुद्धो वज्रपाणिश्च देवराट्॥ वरुणः पाशभृच्चापि सगदो वा धनेश्वरः। न तु भीष्मः सुसंक्रुद्धः शक्यो जेतुं महाहवे॥
en: Indeed the god of Death wrought up with wrath and shooting whetted shafts from his bow, or the king of the celestial armed with the thunder-bolt, or Varuna holding his mighty in noose or the god of wealth wielding his mace, may be vanquished in battle. But Bhishma cnraged in battle could not be vanquished.

sa: स तैः परिवृतः शूरो धार्तराष्ट्रमहारथैः। ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि कार्ष्णिः पञ्चरथान् प्रति॥
en: Though surrounded by those greatest carwarriors of Dhritarashtra's army, the heroic son of Arjuna still showered, on those five carwarriors, a down pour of arrows.

sa: यथाऽऽह भरतश्रेष्ठ नारदस्तत् तथा कुरु। एतद्धि परमं श्रेयो लोकानां भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best among Bharata's race, do as Narada has spoken to you, for this, O best among the Bharatas, is highly beneficial to all creatures.

sa: न तु त्वामनृतुं कर्तुमुत्सहे स्वात्मगौरवात्। अयुध्यमानः साहाय्यं यथोक्तं कुरु माधव॥
en: For my own glorification, I dare not falsify your words; so do you render me assistance, O Madhava, as promised, without fighting on my behalf.

sa: तत्र देवर्षयः सिद्धाश्चारणाश्च समागताः। प्रेक्षन्त तद् रणं घोरं देवासुरसमं भुवि॥
en: The celestial Rishis, the Siddhas and Charanas who were present, saw that battle as if it were the battle between the gods and the demons.

sa: विमुक्तशस्त्रकवचा भीष्मस्य सदनं प्रति। प्रविश्य च तदा भीष्मं शिरोभिः प्रणिपेदिरे॥
en: Towards the tent of Bhishma, having previously cast off their armours and dresses. Then entering the tent, they all touched his feet with their hands.

sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्रूहि तस्मादुपायं नो यथा युद्धे जयेमहि॥ भवन्तं समरे क्रुद्धं दण्डहस्तमिवान्तकम्।
en: Yudhishthira said Tell us the means by which we may be able to vanquish your enraged self in battle-you who resemble the vely god of Death himself wielding the mace.

sa: एवं ब्रुवाणं देवर्षि नृपतिः सृञ्जयोऽब्रवीत्। ममेयं भगवन् कन्या मत्तो वरमभीप्सति॥
en: Thereupon king Srinjaya replied to the celestial sage who spoke those words, thus-"O almighty Rishis, this damsel is my daughter and she solicits my blessings."

sa: तां नीरीक्ष्याब्रवीद् वाक्यं पर्वतः प्रहसन्निव। कस्येयं चञ्जलापानी सर्वलक्षणसम्मता॥
en: Beholding that girl, Parvata smilingly said these words to Srinjaya-"Whose daughter is this girl of restless glances and auspicious marks?

sa: सुदक्षिणं तु राजेन्द्र काम्बोजानां महारथम्। श्रुतकर्मा पराक्रान्तमभ्यद्रवत संयुगे॥
en: O great king, Shrutakarma attacked in that battle the great car warrior, the mighty Sudakshina, the king of the Kambojas.

sa: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा यमाभ्यां सहितः प्रभुः। प्रययौ सिंहनादेन नादयन् भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then king Yudhishthira that mighty lord, with his twin brothers, Nakula and Sahadeva, proceeded to battle, O foremost of the Bharata, uttering his war-cries aloud.

sa: एवमुक्त्वा ययौ कन्या रोषव्याकुललोचना। तापस्ये धृतसंकल्या सा मे चिन्तयती वधम्॥
en: Having spoken thus, that maid went away with eyes agitated with wrath, and intending to bring about my death she firmly resolved to practice asceticism,

sa: उलूक मद्वचो ब्रूहि असकृद्भीमसेनकम्। विराटनगरे पार्थ यस्त्वं सूदो ह्यभूः पुरा॥
en: O Uluka, say on my behalf, to that vicious weight Bhimasena: “O son of Pritha, in the city of Virata were you before a cook,"

sa: स्मयमानश्च देवेशो लोकान् सर्वानवेक्ष्य च। लोकास्त्वासन् यथापूर्वे दृष्टास्तेनापमन्युना॥
en: Then turning his eyes upon the creatures he smiled. Then the creatures lived cheerfully as before, undisturbed by premature death.

sa: व्यभ्राजेतां ततस्तौ तु संयुगे शरविक्षतौ। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे बलशक्रौ महाबलौ॥
en: Wounded with arrows they appeared in the battle like the mighty Indra and the powerful Bala in the battle between the celestial and the Danavas.

sa: भीष्म उवाच ततस्ते तापसाः सर्वे तपसे धृतनिश्चयाम्। दृष्ट्वा न्यवर्तयंस्तात् किं कार्यमिति चाब्रुवन्॥
en: Bhishma said to Then all the ascetics (living in Vatsabhumi), perceiving her firmly resolved on practicing austerities, dissuaded her, and they said "O child, what do you mean to do?"

sa: चेदिराजस्तु संक्रुद्धो बाह्रीकं नवभिः शरैः। विव्याध समरे तूर्णं मत्तो मत्तमिव द्विपम्॥ तौ तत्र समरे क्रुद्धौ नर्दन्तौ च पुनः पुनः। समीयतुः सुसंक्रुद्धावङ्गारकबुधाविव॥ राक्षसं रौद्रकर्माणं क्रूरकर्मा घटोत्कचः। अलम्बुषं प्रत्युदियाद् बलं शक्र इवाहवे॥
en: The king of the Chedis, then becoming exceedingly, angry, quickly pierced Balhika with nine arrows in that battle. Like an infuriated elephants, attacking another infuriated elephants, they roared against each other in great anger. They fought in great wrath and they looked like the planets Angaraka and Budha. Ghatotkacha the barbarous monster attacked on the monster known as Alambusha, the evildoer. This attack was made same way as Indra invaded on Bala, a dangerous demon.

sa: तामुवाच महादेवः कन्यां किल वृषध्वजः। न मे वागनृतं प्राह सत्य भद्रे भविष्यति॥
en: To that maiden Mahadeva (the great god) having the bull for his carrier thus spoke truly, “My words can not be false. They shall turn out true, O blessed one.

sa: रुद्र उवाच संहारार्थे प्रसीदस्व मा रुषो वसुधाधिप। मा प्रजाः स्थावराश्चैव जंगमाश्च व्यनीनशः॥
en: Rudra said Be propitiated, O ruler of the universe and do not cherish wrath for the destruction of creatures. Do you not any longer destroy the mobile and immobile creatures.

sa: चितां कृत्वा सुमहतीं प्रदाय च हुताशनम्। प्रदीप्तेऽग्नौ महाराज रोषदीप्तेन चेतसा॥
en: And making a large funeral pyre and having set fire (to it), O monarch, with a mind burning with wrath, even in that flaming fire,

sa: दुःशासनो महाराज भयं त्यक्त्वा महारथः॥ भीष्मस्य जीविताकाक्षि धनंजयमुपाद्रवत्।
en: Then, O mighty monarch, the great carwarrior Dushasana, desirous of saying Bhishma's confronted Dhananjaya, dismissing all fear from his mind.

sa: संजय उवाच तं तथा परिपृच्छन्तं कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। आश्वासनमिदं वाक्यमुवाच भगवानृषिः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then that illustrious sage spoke these comforting words to Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, who had been questioning him in the above manner.
